news.headline: Perimeter Medical Imaging AI to Participate in the Planet MicroCap Showcase in Toronto
news.summary: CEO Adrian Mendes will present a commercial strategy and milestone update at the Planet MicroCap Showcase in Toronto on October 28, 2026 at 3:30 p.m. ET (webcast live and archived on the IR site), alongside in-person one-on-one investor meetings. It is an investor-conference notice rather than new commercial or reimbursement news.

news.headline: TIME names Perimeter's Claire OCT System a special mention on its Best Inventions of 2026 list
news.summary: TIME recognized Claire, the only FDA-approved imaging device that uses AI during breast-conserving surgery for real-time margin assessment, with a special mention in its Best Inventions of 2026 collection, citing Intermountain surgeon feedback that the AI acts as 'an additional set of trained eyes.' It is a visibility boost for hospital sales conversations but came with no new placement, revenue or reimbursement news.

news.headline: Perimeter Medical Imaging AI Appoints Finance Executive Michelle Caron to Board of Directors
news.summary: Michelle Caron, CPA, currently CFO of Nasdaq-listed A10 Networks and previously CFO at Danaher units Beckman Coulter Life Sciences, Pall and Phenomenex, joined the board effective immediately, adding 28 years of medtech and life-science finance experience. CEO Adrian Mendes framed the hire around scaling commercial operations and advancing Claire; the release contained no reimbursement or revenue news, making this the first company announcement of any kind since the August 20 Q2 print.

news.headline: MicroCap Opportunities: 'First Two Claires and the Reimbursement Clock'
news.summary: A detailed post-Q2 breakdown notes both installed Claire systems are S-Series conversions at Intermountain's LDS Hospital and American Fork rather than net-new customers, leaving the site count stuck at 22 with no upfront capital-sale revenue. It frames Q2's US$503K revenue, the 28% opex cut and US$6.4M cash (about 12 months of runway) as a race between the commercial ramp and the CMS reimbursement clock.

news.headline: Perimeter Announces Preliminary Second Quarter 2026 Financial Results
news.summary: Q2 2026 revenue was about US$503K, all recurring (S-Series consumables, leases, maintenance) and flat versus US$506K a year ago though up 31% sequentially from Q1's US$385K, while operating expenses fell 28% year-over-year to US$3.1M and the net loss narrowed to US$2.6M from US$3.9M. Cash stood at US$6.4M at June 30, and the release highlighted the first two Claire placements as S-Series replacements at two top-tier hospitals.

news.headline: Q2 2026 earnings call: 2-3x revenue growth target held, funnel 'in flux', HCPCS application under CMS review
news.summary: CEO Adrian Mendes confirmed only two commercial Claire installs, both S-Series conversions, and declined to quantify a funnel he called 'in flux' as hospital AI review committees push some deals toward 2027. CFO Sara Brien reiterated roughly 12 months of runway, and management said the HCPCS coding application filed with CMS in June is under review, guiding to first Medicare claims in Q1 2027.

catalysts.label: Q3 2026 results - first full quarter of Claire commercialization
catalysts.detail: The Q3 print is the first full reporting period after the August Intermountain go-live and the first look at Claire-related revenue and gross margin against the roughly US$2M annualized S-Series base, plus the next hard update on cash burn after the US$6.4M June 30 balance. Market calendars point to around November 12-17 (Q3 2025 came on November 12); Perimeter usually announces the call date about a week in advance.

catalysts.label: CMS preliminary HCPCS determination for Claire (B2 2026 public meeting)
catalysts.detail: Perimeter filed its HCPCS Level II application in June 2026, which under CMS's biannual non-drug schedule (July 1 deadline) falls into the B2 2026 cycle. In that cycle CMS posts preliminary coding determinations ahead of a public meeting held in mid-December (B2 2025 met December 17-18), making December the first public read on whether Claire gets a dedicated code. This is the single biggest binary item on the calendar.

catalysts.label: First net-new Claire placement outside the legacy base
catalysts.detail: Both commercial Claire systems are conversions of existing S-Series customers on a flat 22-site base, carrying no upfront capital-sale revenue. A genuinely new hospital system signing is the clearest proof the Intermountain deal is repeatable; management cites late-stage opportunities but will not size the funnel, blaming hospital AI review committees for delays. Nothing has been announced as of October 22, seven months after FDA approval.

catalysts.label: Roll-out across the wider Intermountain Health network
catalysts.detail: Claire is live at only two Intermountain hospitals (LDS Hospital and American Fork Hospital) despite a systemwide agreement covering a much larger network, and no further sites have been announced since the August 13 go-live. Expansion would show the flagship customer scales rather than stalling at a two-site footprint and would lift per-procedure consumable revenue, the recurring part of the model.

catalysts.label: Delivery on the 2-3x FY2026 revenue growth target
catalysts.detail: Management reaffirmed 2-3x revenue growth for 2026 but conceded deals could slip into 2027. With H1 revenue of about US$0.89M against FY2025 revenue of US$2.3M, the target implies an extremely back-loaded Q4 built on capital sales that have not yet been signed - a hard test of the commercial ramp and of management credibility, with the verdict landing at the FY2026 print in March 2027.

catalysts.label: HCPCS code effective date and first Medicare claims
catalysts.detail: CMS's published schedule makes B2-cycle codes effective in April of the following year, i.e. around April 1, 2027 - later than management's guidance for first Medicare and Medicare Advantage claims in Q1 2027, so the reimbursement unlock may slip by a quarter. A dedicated code is the precondition for hospital billing and for commercial payers opening medical policy reviews.

catalysts.label: Next financing round
catalysts.detail: Cash stood at US$6.4M on June 30 with roughly 12 months of runway, following the C$7.52M LIFE offering at C$0.35 and C$6.04M of convertible debentures closed in June. With the shares around C$0.20, well below that issue price, a further raise is likely before the HCPCS code is effective and would be materially dilutive unless a new customer signing or a positive coding decision re-rates the stock first. The October addition of a sitting public-company CFO to the board reads as preparation for that step.

pulse: PINK last closed at about US$0.118 on the OTC (PYNKF) on October 23, down from roughly US$0.13 and still near the bottom of its 52-week range, well below the C$0.35 LIFE issue price. No new company news has appeared since the October 22 Planet MicroCap notice, so there is still no net-new hospital, no Intermountain expansion beyond two sites and no reimbursement update. That makes the October 28 Toronto presentation the near-term watch point for funnel commentary. With US$6.4M of cash at June 30 (about a year of runway) and a likely dilutive raise ahead, the swing factors remain the Q3 print (not yet scheduled, estimated around mid-November) and the December CMS public meeting on the HCPCS code.
